scope: Proposition 3.4 of the manuscript “Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A2” (preprints/Elliptic-Squares-and-Zilber-Pink-for-Curves-in-A2-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d3ecf115570d0b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the fixed finite collection (3.2), only finitely many coarse Hecke correspondences admit a dominating relation between a pair of these curves. In particular there is a fixed finite list T containing every exceptional joint image in Proposition 3.3. We may take this list closed under exchanging the two factors and choose, for every member, positive integral multipliers for isogenies realizing all its pairs. The list and these multipliers are fixed before any additional auxiliary levels are chosen.
